default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-538.title: Day-open revisit hold
E-538.hypothesis: After trading on one side of the session open for a while, a bar that dips back to the open and closes on the original side shows the open price defended by that side's buyers/sellers; follow the original side.

E-539.title: Prior-session open rejection
E-539.hypothesis: The previous session's opening print is a reference few systems track; a poke into it from one side that closes back is rejected supply/demand; fade it.

E-540.title: VWAP-deviation time-of-day z fade
E-540.hypothesis: A distance from VWAP large compared with what this minute of the day usually shows is a stretch that mean-reverting liquidity providers fade once the bar turns.

E-541.title: Bar-colour share extreme fade
E-541.hypothesis: When nearly all recent bars have closed the same colour, aggressive flow is spent and the first bar count reaching the extreme share marks a point where the move is crowded; fade it.

E-542.title: Realized-volatility surge direction follow
E-542.hypothesis: A jump in short-window realized volatility above this time of day's norm signals new information arriving; informed flow keeps pushing in the direction of the move that caused it.

E-543.title: Midday-price cross follow
E-543.hypothesis: The price at a fixed midday clock mark is where the morning's positions are balanced; a held close beyond it in the afternoon shifts the balance and the new side keeps control.

E-544.title: Opening-range midpoint hold
E-544.hypothesis: The midpoint of the opening range is the opening auction's fair value; sustained closes beyond it after the range completes show which side won the opening and tend to continue.

E-545.title: Volume-trough bar break
E-545.hypothesis: A bar with the lowest volume in a while means resting liquidity thinned out; the next bar that breaks its high or low finds little opposition and follows through.

E-546.title: Opening-volume-backed range break
E-546.hypothesis: A session whose opening range traded much more volume than recent opening ranges has strong participation; a break of that range is backed by real flow and continues.

E-547.title: Momentum hook after an extreme
E-547.hypothesis: After an outsized counter move, momentum turning back through zero marks forced liquidations ending; trade the turn.
